| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host

| order by files desc

NodeBB Patches Eight AI-Found Flaws Exposing Admin Access and Private Chats

The Hacker News
2026-07-24 16 use cases 7 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Eight security flaws in NodeBB went public on Wednesday, along with the code to exploit them. Aikido Security rates all eight as high severity and says its AI pentest agents found them in a six-hour review of the forum software's source code. Every version before 4.14.0 is affected. NodeBB has fixed them all, and administrators should be on 4.14.2. The simplest one takes a settings change. A

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] NodeBB federation actor spoofing (CVE-2026-58593): external POST to ActivityPub inbox · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] NodeBB privilege escalation: non-admin reaching /api/admin/* after homePageCustom bypass · [LLM] NodeBB i18n translation-token XSS: [[topic:merged-message,...]] injected in request URI · Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → Suspicious browser extension installation
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] NodeBB unauthenticated private-data enumeration via ActivityPub outbox / message endpoints · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
NodeBB privilege escalation: non-admin reaching /api/admin/* after homePageCustom bypass AIExploitation Medium
Hunts NodeBB's client-side-only admin block bypass (pre-4.14.0), where a regular member points the homePageCustom setting at /admin and then loads admin-only routes. Surfaces HTTP 200 responses on /admin and /api/admin/* (error log, user CSV export, logo upload, category management) so an analyst can confirm whether the requesting account/IP is actually an administrator. Rationale: Uses the exact admin routes the Aikido writeup names as reachable via the homePageCustom client-side bypass (/api/admin/advanced/errors, /api/admin/users/csv, /api/admin/uploadlogo). Hunting tier because web access logs lack the requester's forum role, so the analyst confirms non-admin identity. Defender/Falcon/Datadog/CloudWatch empty: no inbound HTTP-request path telemetry exists in those sources. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/eight-high-severity-vulnerabilities-nodebb • https://cybersecuritynews.com/eight-nodebb-vulnerabilities/
ATT&CKT1190 T1548
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate forum administrator using the admin dashboard
  • Uptime/synthetic monitoring probing /admin health endpoints
  • CI/CD or plugin health checks hitting /api/admin/*
  • Backup jobs pulling /api/admin/users/csv on schedule
Suppression filter
| where CsUsername !in ("admin", "nodebb-admin") and CIp !in ("10.0.0.0/8")
Response runbook
1) Triage: resolve CIp/CsUsername to a forum account and confirm whether it holds an admin/global-moderator role; a member or unauthenticated session reaching /api/admin/* = true positive. 2) Contain: force-logout the account, reset its session/token, and confirm NodeBB is upgraded to 4.14.2 (client-side-only block is fixed server-side there). 3) Hunt: review that source IP for prior PUT /api/v3/users/*/settings changing homePageCustom to /admin, and for logo/category/user-export changes made under the bypass.
AppServiceHTTPLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where CsUriStem == "/admin" or CsUriStem startswith "/admin/" or CsUriStem startswith "/api/admin/"
| where ScStatus in (200, 201)
| summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated), Hits=count(), Paths=make_set(CsUriStem, 25), Methods=make_set(CsMethod, 5) by CIp, UserAgent, CsUsername
| order by FirstSeen desc

NodeBB i18n translation-token XSS: [[topic:merged-message,...]] injected in request URI AIExploitation High
Hunts NodeBB's second-pass translation XSS (pre-4.14.0, the 325-file rebuild in 4.14.0). User input containing NodeBB translator tokens ([[ / %5B%5B / topic:merged-message) is smuggled into a page and executed on the translation pass. Flags requests whose URL or query string carries these translator markers, including the /flags?quick= reflected sink. Rationale: NodeBB's translator uses the [[namespace:key,args]] syntax; the writeup's PoC is literally /flags?quick=]][[topic:merged-message,javascript:alert(origin). Matching [[ / %5B%5B / topic:merged-message in the URI is a precise attack signature with near-zero legitimate use in query strings. contains (not has) is used deliberately — the bracket sequences are not token-aligned. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/eight-high-severity-vulnerabilities-nodebb • https://cyberpress.org/nodebb-patches-eight-high-severity-flaws/
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.007
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer/QA testing i18n rendering with literal [[ tokens
  • Security scanners (Burp, ZAP, Nuclei) probing for XSS with bracket payloads
  • Legitimate deep links that happen to contain double square brackets in a parameter
  • Translation plugin admin previewing a translation key
Suppression filter
| where UserAgent !has_any ("nuclei", "zap", "burp", "nikto") and CsUsername !in ("qa", "i18n-admin")
Response runbook
1) Triage: decode CsUriQuery and check for a translator key chained to a script sink (javascript:, onerror, alert(origin)); confirm ScStatus 200 (payload reflected/stored). 2) Contain: block the source IP at the WAF, purge any forum post/flag containing the token, and verify upgrade to 4.14.2 which rebuilt the translation pass. 3) Hunt: search post bodies and /flags?quick=, /topic, and profile fields for stored [[ tokens; review UrlClickEvents/proxy logs for victims who loaded the injected page.
AppServiceHTTPLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where CsUriQuery contains "[[" or CsUriQuery contains "%5B%5B" or CsUriQuery contains "topic:merged-message" or CsUriStem contains "[[" or CsUriStem contains "%5B%5B"
| project TimeGenerated, CIp, CsMethod, CsUriStem, CsUriQuery, ScStatus, UserAgent, CsUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc

NodeBB federation actor spoofing (CVE-2026-58593): external POST to ActivityPub inbox AIDelivery Medium
Hunts inbound ActivityPub delivery abused by CVE-2026-58593 and the Aikido federation flaws, where a remote server posts to a NodeBB inbox and NodeBB fails to bind attributedTo to the authenticated actor, letting an outside server author posts/DMs as any local uid (including admin). Surfaces external POSTs to /category/*/inbox, /uid/*/inbox and /ap/inbox/* so rare/new peer instances can be reviewed. Rationale: CVE-2026-58593 (CVSS 8.7, corroborated on NVD) lets a remote actor set attributedTo to a bare uid (e.g. 1 = admin) on objects posted to the inbox routes the Aikido writeup enumerates (/category/*/inbox, /uid/*/inbox, /ap/inbox/*). Access logs rarely capture the JSON body, so this baselines external inbox POSTs by peer; new/rare source IPs are the pivot. Requires federation enabled. Cross-checked against: • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-58593 • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/eight-high-severity-vulnerabilities-nodebb
ATT&CKT1190 T1656
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate Mastodon/ActivityPub peer instances delivering to your inbox
  • Relay servers fanning out activities to category inboxes
  • Federation load/health checks from a known partner instance
  • Your own forum's outbound-then-inbound reply threads
Response runbook
1) Triage: for the source IP, pull the inbox POST body from WAF/app logs (if captured) and check whether attributedTo/object.actor matches the HTTP-Signature keyId actor; a mismatch (e.g. attributedTo: 1) = spoofing. 2) Contain: defederate/block the offending instance domain and IP, disable federation if not required, and upgrade to 4.14.2. 3) Hunt: review recent posts/DMs authored by admin or high-privilege uids for content that arrived via federation, and correlate against unknown peer domains in /.well-known/webfinger and /ap/actor/* lookups.
AppServiceHTTPLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where CsMethod == "POST"
| where CsUriStem endswith "/inbox" and (CsUriStem startswith "/category/" or CsUriStem startswith "/uid/" or CsUriStem startswith "/ap/inbox/")
| summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated), Posts=count(), Endpoints=make_set(CsUriStem, 25) by CIp, UserAgent
| order by FirstSeen desc

NodeBB unauthenticated private-data enumeration via ActivityPub outbox / message endpoints AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the two no-account NodeBB flaws that leak private data: reading private messages one-at-a-time (/message/:mid) and dumping private-category contents (/category/:cid/outbox) to any requester. Flags a single client fetching many distinct message/outbox objects — the enumeration pattern the article describes ('one at a time'). Rationale: Targets the exact endpoints the writeup names for the unauthenticated private-message read (/message/:mid) and private-category disclosure (/category/:cid/outbox). The >5 distinct-object threshold captures the 'one at a time' enumeration while a single legitimate fetch won't trip it. Sigma omitted: this is an aggregation/threshold rule, not single-event shape. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/eight-high-severity-vulnerabilities-nodebb • https://cybersecuritynews.com/eight-nodebb-vulnerabilities/
ATT&CKT1190 T1213
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate ActivityPub peers pulling public category outboxes
  • Search-engine or archive crawlers walking message/topic URLs
  • A logged-in power user legitimately reading many of their own DMs
  • Internal migration/export tooling iterating over objects
Suppression filter
| where UserAgent !has_any ("Mastodon", "friendica", "bot", "crawler", "spider")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the source IP/UA is unauthenticated (no valid session) and that the fetched /message/ or /category/*/outbox objects belong to private conversations/categories; volume of distinct IDs indicates scraping. 2) Contain: block the IP at the WAF, rotate any secrets exposed in leaked DMs, and upgrade to 4.14.2 which adds the missing authorization checks on the side routes. 3) Hunt: pivot on the same IP/UA for /.well-known/webfinger, /ap/actor/* and /uid/*/inbox activity indicating a full federation-based recon-and-read chain.

| where CsUriStem startswith "/message/" or (CsUriStem startswith "/category/" and CsUriStem endswith "/outbox")

| where DistinctObjects > 5
| order by DistinctObjects desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process Exploitation High
Classic macro/exploit pattern — Office app launching cmd/powershell/wmic/regsvr32.

DeviceProcessEvents

| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\winword.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\excel.exe"

   or ParentProcessName endswith "\outlook.exe"

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.
ATT&CKT1528 T1098.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d05

APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime

    where Authentication.action="success"
      AND Authentication.signature IN (

| `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication
    where Authentication.action="success"
      AND Authentication.signature IN (
        "Consent to application",
        "Add app role assignment grant to user",

    by Authentication.user, Authentication.app, Authentication.src, Authentication.signature
| `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)`
Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: LSASS Process Access Outside Microsoft-Signed Tooling
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d04
status: experimental
description: |
    Anything opening lsass.exe with read-memory access that isn't a
    Microsoft signed component (Defender, csrss, etc.) is suspect.
    Mimikatz / Pypykatz / nanodump signature.
references:

author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1003.001
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: process_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetImage|endswith: '\lsass.exe'
    filter_known_good:
        SourceImage|endswith:
            - '\MsSense.exe'
            - '\MsMpEng.exe'
            - '\csrss.exe'
            - '\svchost.exe'
            - '\wininit.exe'
            - '\services.exe'

level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__IP_LIST__` / `__DOMAIN_LIST__` placeholders with
    article-specific destinations. For dynamic IOC management, use a
    watchlist or external feed.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/tactics/TA0011/

date: 2026/05/02
tags:

    category: network_connection
    product: windows

    selection_ip:

    selection_domain:

            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_2__'

falsepositives:

NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic

    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port

    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("attacker.tld")

     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("attacker.tld")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement

Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-12569")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-12569")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"

                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName

// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("55a1eb4c2d3da04376df39d7ba832569c6af1a37a0cf2b95f754ac898023a30c") or SHA1 in~ ("55a1eb4c2d3da04376df39d7ba832569c6af1a37a0cf2b95f754ac898023a30c") or MD5 in~ ("55a1eb4c2d3da04376df39d7ba832569c6af1a37a0cf2b95f754ac898023a30c")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("55a1eb4c2d3da04376df39d7ba832569c6af1a37a0cf2b95f754ac898023a30c") or SHA1 in~ ("55a1eb4c2d3da04376df39d7ba832569c6af1a37a0cf2b95f754ac898023a30c") or MD5 in~ ("55a1eb4c2d3da04376df39d7ba832569c6af1a37a0cf2b95f754ac898023a30c")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["55a1eb4c2d3da04376df39d7ba832569c6af1a37a0cf2b95f754ac898023a30c"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Kimi K3 Agents Found Redis Zero-Days and Built RCE Exploit, Researchers Say

The Hacker News
2026-07-24 13 use cases 7 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

Redis shipped seven security releases on July 23 after researchers published authenticated RCE PoCs for stock Redis 6.2.22, 7.4.9, 8.6.4, and 8.8.0. All four chains require RESTORE. The Streams chains also need EVAL and XGROUP; the 8.8.0 chain needs EVAL and the bundled RedisBloom module. Redis says the underlying memory flaws may lead to remote code execution. redis-server process spawns a shell/interpreter (RESTORE-chain system() RCE payoff) AIExploitation High
Hunts the terminal step common to all four published Redis RCE chains (6.2.22/7.4.9/8.6.4 Streams shared-NACK and 8.8.0 RedisBloom TDigest): after corrupting memory via RESTORE the exploit poisons a hash function so a crafted GET/command invokes system(), making the redis-server daemon the parent of /bin/sh or another interpreter. A production Redis server never legitimately forks a shell, so this is a near-zero-FP signal of successful exploitation. Rationale: Every chain in the article and PoC repo converges on invoking system() from redis-server, so redis-server parenting a shell is the highest-fidelity observable. Parent=redis-server + child interpreter is the article-specific pivot, not a generic shell-spawn. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/berabuddies/redis-poc • https://redis.io/blog/security-advisory-cve202623479-cve202625243-cve-2026-25588-cve202625589-cve-2026-23631/ • https://securityonline.info/redis-rce-vulnerabilities-memory-corruption-restore-command-patch/ • https://www.zeroday.cloud/blog/redis-cve-2026-25243-deep-dive
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Redis Docker image using docker-entrypoint.sh where redis-server is briefly reparented as PID1 and reaps child helper scripts
  • Operator running `redis-cli --eval` diagnostics on the host that a naive parser mis-attributes to redis-server
  • Backup/monitoring sidecars that wrap redis-server startup in a shell supervisor (parent is the wrapper, not redis-server — verify parent binary)
  • Custom Redis modules that legitimately shell out for maintenance jobs
  • Redis BGSAVE/AOF-rewrite forking a child redis-server (redis-server child, not a shell — excluded by the interpreter allowlist)
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("docker-entrypoint","/usr/local/bin/docker-entrypoint.sh"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the child ProcessCommandLine and grandchildren on the host; a reverse shell, curl|bash, or recon string (id/uname/whoami) confirms RCE. Check redis-server uptime and ACL config for who holds RESTORE/EVAL/XGROUP. 2) Contain: isolate the host, kill the redis-server child tree, and firewall Redis (6379/TLS 6380) from untrusted networks; rotate the requirepass/ACL secrets. 3) Hunt: check the exact Redis branch version against fixed releases (6.2.23/7.2.15/7.4.10/8.2.8/8.4.5/8.6.5/8.8.1), review other Redis nodes for the same parent-shell pattern, and search syslog for redis-server crash/BUG REPORT entries around the same timestamp.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "redis-server"
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","zsh","ksh","python","python3","perl","nc","ncat","socat","curl","wget")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has "redis-server"
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("bash","dash","zsh","ksh","python","perl","socat","ncat","curl","wget") or ActingProcessName endswith "/sh" or ActingProcessName == "sh"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Unpatched Redis version exposure to RESTORE-chain RCE (branch-exact) AIExploitation High
Surfaces hosts running Redis builds vulnerable to the July 2026 Streams shared-NACK and RedisBloom/TDigest RESTORE RCE chains by comparing the exact installed version against the per-branch fixed releases (6.2.23/7.2.15/7.4.10/8.2.8/8.4.5/8.6.5/8.8.1). The article stresses checking the exact branch version, not whether Redis was 'recently patched' — 6.2.22 and 7.4.9 were the May destination yet remained exploitable. Rationale: Uses the article's exact fixed-release list per branch to compute vulnerable ranges, catching the four PoC-confirmed builds (6.2.22/7.4.9/8.6.4/8.8.0) plus every other pre-fix build — an inventory-precise, non-generic exposure hunt. Cross-checked against: • https://redis.io/blog/security-advisory-cve202623479-cve202625243-cve-2026-25588-cve202625589-cve-2026-23631/ • https://github.com/berabuddies/redis-poc • https://cybersecuritynews.com/redis-vulnerabilities-enables-rce/
ATT&CKT1190
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Redis fork/derivative (Valkey, KeyDB, Redis Stack) reporting a Redis-like version string that doesn't map to these branches
  • Air-gapped/internal-only Redis where RESTORE is already ACL-revoked (still shows as vulnerable version but not reachable)
  • Vendor-backported build whose reported version predates the fix but contains the patch (rare, verify with vendor)
  • TVM snapshot lag showing a version already upgraded in the last 24h
  • Development/test containers intentionally pinned to old Redis for regression testing
Suppression filter
| where SoftwareName !has "valkey" and SoftwareName !has "keydb"
Response runbook
1) Triage: for each flagged host confirm the Redis is authenticated-reachable and whether ACL users hold RESTORE (and EVAL/XGROUP, or RedisBloom for 8.8.0); internet-facing + RESTORE-enabled = critical. 2) Contain: as interim mitigation revoke RESTORE from non-essential ACL accounts (`ACL SETUSER ... -restore`) and block untrusted network access to 6379/6380; schedule upgrade to the branch's fixed release. 3) Hunt: pivot flagged hosts into UC1 (redis-server child shell) and UC2 (crash logs) to check whether any were already exploited; expand inventory to Redis running in containers/K8s not covered by endpoint TVM.

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count

          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d07
status: experimental
description: |
    Word/Excel/Outlook/OneNote spawning powershell, cmd, wscript,
    cscript, mshta, rundll32, regsvr32 — classic macro / embedded-
    object payload signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059
    - attack.t1566.001
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\winword.exe'
            - '\excel.exe'
            - '\powerpnt.exe'
            - '\outlook.exe'
            - '\onenote.exe'
            - '\mspub.exe'
            - '\visio.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate automation macros in trusted internal documents
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.
ATT&CKT1528 T1098.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

references:

author: Clankerusecase

    product: azure
    service: auditlogs

        OperationName: 'Consent to application'

APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication
    where Authentication.action="success"
      AND Authentication.signature IN (
        "Consent to application",
        "Add app role assignment grant to user",
        "Add OAuth2PermissionGrant",
        "Add delegated permission grant")
    by Authentication.user, Authentication.app, Authentication.src, Authentication.signature
| `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication
    where Authentication.action="success"
      AND Authentication.signature IN (
        "Consent to application",
        "Add app role assignment grant to user",

    by Authentication.user, Authentication.app, Authentication.src, Authentication.signature
| `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)`
Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: LSASS Process Access Outside Microsoft-Signed Tooling
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d04
status: experimental
description: |
    Anything opening lsass.exe with read-memory access that isn't a
    Microsoft signed component (Defender, csrss, etc.) is suspect.
    Mimikatz / Pypykatz / nanodump signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1003.001
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: process_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetImage|endswith: '\lsass.exe'
    filter_known_good:
        SourceImage|endswith:
            - '\MsSense.exe'
            - '\MsMpEng.exe'
            - '\csrss.exe'
            - '\svchost.exe'
            - '\wininit.exe'
            - '\services.exe'
            - '\lsm.exe'
            - '\SearchProtocolHost.exe'
    condition: selection and not filter_known_good
falsepositives:
    - Third-party EDR / forensic tools — extend the filter list
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

Fake Notepad++ Plugin Delivers MATCHBOIL.V2 in UAC-0099 Attacks

The Hacker News
2026-07-24 20 use cases 10 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

The Computer Emergency Response Team of Ukraine (CERT-UA) has warned of a new campaign that involves the use of a malicious program that's dressed up as a Notepad++ plugin to compromise Windows systems. The activity has been attributed by the agency to a threat cluster it tracks as UAC-0099, a Russia-aligned group that has previously observed weaponizing security flaws in WinRAR software to

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] UAC-0099 fake-PDF VBScript launching Notepad++ / WinRAR (LUNCHPOKE stage) · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Notepad++ side-loading NppExport.dll from a non-Program Files path (LUNCHPOKE) · Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Fake Notepad++ Plugin Delivers MATCHBOIL.V2 in UAC-0099 Attacks
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] WinRAR extracting password-protected updater.rar in UAC-0099 chain · [LLM] Recurring scheduled task running RemoteLibUpdater.exe (BURNYBEAR persistence, 3-min cadence) · Suspicious browser extension installation · Scheduled task created with suspicious image / encoded args
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] BURNYBEAR (RemoteLibUpdater.exe) loading MATCHBOIL.V2 InitTest.dll

Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
UAC-0099 fake-PDF VBScript launching Notepad++ / WinRAR (LUNCHPOKE stage) AIDelivery High
Hunts the UAC-0099 loader stage where a VBScript disguised as a PDF (wscript.exe/cscript.exe) directly spawns the bundled legitimate Notepad++ 8.8.3 or WinRAR from an extracted directory. Legitimate Notepad++/WinRAR are effectively never launched by a script host, making this parent→child pair high-fidelity for the initial execution. Rationale: wscript/cscript → notepad++.exe|winrar.exe is a parent/child pair with near-zero legitimate occurrence; the article states the fake-PDF VBS 'extract the contents of the archive and launch Notepad++'. Anchored on named binaries, not a generic script-spawn template. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/hackers-abuse-notepad-plus-plus-plugins-to-stealthily-install-malware/ • https://securityaffairs.com/195923/cyber-warfare-2/uac-0099-is-now-hiding-malware-inside-a-fake-notepad-plugin-to-target-ukrainian-organizations.html
ATT&CKT1059.005 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Software packaging/deployment scripts (SCCM, PDQ) that call winrar.exe from a VBS wrapper
  • Legacy admin logon scripts that launch text editors
  • Custom VBS installers bundled by a helpdesk that unpack with WinRAR
  • Portable-app launchers that shell out to notepad++.exe
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("\\SCCM\\","\\PDQ","deploy") and InitiatingProcessFolderPath has "\\Windows\\")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the parent VBS path and command line; confirm the .vbs sits in a user-writable/extracted dir (Downloads, %TEMP%, random-named folder) and check whether a decoy PDF opened simultaneously. 2) Contain: isolate the host, kill the wscript/cscript and child trees, and quarantine the source ZIP/VBS and any Evernote.zip. 3) Hunt: on the same host look for NppExport.dll side-loading, winrar.exe extracting updater.rar, and a scheduled task running RemoteLibUpdater.exe every 3 minutes.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("notepad++.exe","winrar.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("notepad++.exe","winrar.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: VBScript Host Spawning Notepad++ or WinRAR (UAC-0099 LUNCHPOKE)
id: 6f2c1a4e-3b7d-4c1a-9e0f-2a5d8c1b7e40
description: Detects wscript.exe/cscript.exe launching Notepad++ or WinRAR, as seen in the UAC-0099 fake Notepad++ plugin chain.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/fake-notepad-plugin-delivers.html
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/hackers-abuse-notepad-plus-plus-plugins-to-stealthily-install-malware/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/07/27
tags:

  - attack.t1204.002
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
    Image|endswith:
      - '\notepad++.exe'
      - '\winrar.exe'
  condition: selection
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\wscript.exe OR *\Wscript.exe OR *\WScript.exe OR *\cscript.exe OR *\CScript.exe) @Image:(*\notepad++.exe OR *\Notepad++.exe OR *\winrar.exe OR *\WinRAR.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/(wscript|cscript)\.exe$/i
| ImageFileName=/\\(notepad\+\+|winrar)\.exe$/i
| table([_time, aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine])
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe")) AND (Processes.process_name IN ("notepad++.exe","winrar.exe")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe")) AND (Processes.process_name IN ("notepad++.exe","winrar.exe")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Notepad++ side-loading NppExport.dll from a non-Program Files path (LUNCHPOKE) AIExploitation High
Hunts the DLL side-load core of the UAC-0099 chain: a copy of Notepad++ 8.8.3 running from a randomly-named extracted directory loading a malicious NppExport.dll (LUNCHPOKE) instead of the genuine plugin under Program Files. The pivot is location — legitimate NppExport.dll only ever loads from the installed plugins directory. Rationale: Anchors on the exact malicious plugin name NppExport.dll plus a location predicate: the genuine plugin only loads from the Program Files Notepad++ plugins folder, so a load from a random extracted directory is the side-load itself. Falcon/Sentinel fall back to notepad++.exe executing outside Program Files since image-load isn't in the provided FDR/Sentinel schema. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/hackers-abuse-notepad-plus-plus-plugins-to-stealthily-install-malware/ • https://gbhackers.com/hackers-weaponize-notepad-plugins/
ATT&CKT1574.002 T1036
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Portable Notepad++ builds run from a USB stick or user profile with a bundled export plugin
  • Developers running a self-compiled Notepad++ from a build/output directory
  • Notepad++ installed per-user under %LOCALAPPDATA% rather than Program Files
  • Software-testing sandboxes that stage Notepad++ in a temp folder
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("\\Portable","\\Notepad++Portable","\\Dev\\","\\build\\"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: hash the loaded NppExport.dll and compare to the known-good Notepad++ 8.8.3 plugin hash; inspect its parent directory for winrar.exe, updater.rar and Evernote.zip siblings. 2) Contain: isolate the host and quarantine the whole extracted directory (Notepad++ copy + DLL + RAR). 3) Hunt: pivot to any scheduled task launching RemoteLibUpdater.exe and to RemoteLibUpdater.exe loading InitTest.dll.
DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "notepad++.exe"
| where FileName =~ "NppExport.dll"
| where FolderPath !startswith "C:\\Program Files"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\notepad++.exe"
| where not(NewProcessName startswith "C:\\Program Files")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, ParentProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Notepad++ Side-Loading NppExport.dll From Non-Standard Path (UAC-0099)
id: 2b9e7d31-6c48-4f2a-8a1c-5d0f9b3e6a12
description: Detects notepad++.exe loading NppExport.dll from outside the installed Program Files plugins directory, matching UAC-0099 LUNCHPOKE side-loading.

  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/hackers-abuse-notepad-plus-plus-plugins-to-stealthily-install-malware/

source:windows.sysmon @EventID:7 @Image:(*\notepad++.exe OR *\Notepad++.exe) @ImageLoaded:(*\NppExport.dll OR *\nppexport.dll OR *\NPPEXPORT.DLL) -@ImageLoaded:(*\Program Files\* OR *\Program Files (x86)\*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\notepad\+\+\.exe$/i

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="notepad++.exe" AND NOT (Processes.process_path IN ("C:\\Program Files\\Notepad++\\*","C:\\Program Files (x86)\\Notepad++\\*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process_path Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="notepad++.exe" AND NOT (Processes.process_path IN ("C:\\Program Files\\Notepad++\\*","C:\\Program Files (x86)\\Notepad++\\*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process_path Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
WinRAR extracting password-protected updater.rar in UAC-0099 chain AIInstallation High
Hunts LUNCHPOKE unpacking the second-stage payload: the bundled legitimate winrar.exe (or rar.exe) invoked to extract the password-protected updater.rar that contains RemoteLibUpdater.exe (BURNYBEAR) and InitTest.dll (MATCHBOIL.V2). The archive name updater.rar is a campaign-unique anchor. Rationale: updater.rar is a fixed, campaign-specific archive name named in the article; combining it with the extraction utility yields a very low-noise, article-specific detection for the BURNYBEAR/MATCHBOIL.V2 staging step. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/hackers-abuse-notepad-plus-plus-plugins-to-stealthily-install-malware/ • https://cyberpress.org/hackers-weaponize-notepad-8-8-3/
ATT&CKT1140 T1560.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A user coincidentally naming a legitimate archive updater.rar (rare)
  • IT distributing a software 'updater.rar' package via WinRAR
  • Backup tooling archiving to a file that happens to match the name
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFolderPath has "\\Windows\\" and InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("ccmexec.exe","tiworker.exe"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the winrar.exe parent is notepad++.exe or a script host, and that the -p (password) flag or a random destination directory is present; recover the extracted RemoteLibUpdater.exe / InitTest.dll. 2) Contain: isolate the host and quarantine updater.rar and its extracted contents. 3) Hunt: sweep the fleet for updater.rar drops from EasySend/Evernote.zip lineage and for the 3-minute RemoteLibUpdater.exe scheduled task.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("winrar.exe","rar.exe","unrar.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "updater.rar"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName has_any ("winrar.exe","rar.exe","unrar.exe")
| where CommandLine has "updater.rar"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: WinRAR Extracting updater.rar (UAC-0099 BURNYBEAR Staging)
id: 8d41c0a7-72e5-4b19-9f3a-1c7b6e0d2f55
description: Detects winrar.exe/rar.exe extracting the password-protected updater.rar staged by UAC-0099 LUNCHPOKE.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/fake-notepad-plugin-delivers.html
  - https://securityaffairs.com/195923/cyber-warfare-2/uac-0099-is-now-hiding-malware-inside-a-fake-notepad-plugin-to-target-ukrainian-organizations.html
